text:
marta: Quick heads-up — saw a p99 spike on the Triton route during a short-sequence burst (14:03-14:06 UTC). triton_p99 went ~98ms -> 210ms while kv_warm_fraction fell to 0.18. routing_switch_rate ticked up.
chen: Can you paste the model + sample seqlen distro? which workload?
marta: model=gpt-j-8b. seqlen p50=16 p95=64. This traffic had a sudden short-prompt burst from the UI test cluster. KV warm fraction = fraction hitting prefix/KV cache.
aj: Shortseq should usually route to Cutlass. Why did Triton keep getting traffic? routing policy is cost-first with probe bias; maybe probe sampling skewed.
asim: Attaching the lightweight profiler snapshot I grabbed.
asim: ```
# profiler snippet
kernel: triton_attention avg_ms:2.1 p99_ms:45 samples:120
kernel: cutlass_attention avg_ms:1.7 p99_ms:18 samples:86
queue_len:3
kv_lookup_hit:0.18
router_decision:triton (policy=cost_bias, probe=0.05)
``` 
kevin: Notable that triton p99 >> cutlass tail. Tail seems correlated with KV miss/backpressure and kernel preemption on H100. avg is fine but tails blow up.
marta: hypothesis: router smooths seqlen histogram with a 60s window and a low learning rate. during a short burst it didn't adapt fast enough -> probes kept preferring Triton variants. Need hysteresis tweak or faster probe reaction.
chen: Suggest metrics: `router_signal_sensitivity` (how quickly router changes path) and `triton_route_switch_count`. Also consider a short-circuit: prefer Cutlass if kv_warm_fraction < 0.3 AND p99_triton > 150ms.
runtime-bot: canary: router-policy update by aj scheduled 2026-03-10T14:30Z -> will run for 30m
aj: Quick experiment plan: force short sequences -> Cutlass for 30m and compare p95/p99. Command:
`./routerctl set-policy model:gpt-j-8b short-pref=cutlass --ttl 1800`
kevin: Also we should upsample Cutlass probes whenever kv_warm_fraction < 0.4 to avoid probe starvation.
marta: Action items:
  1) aj: run forced-routing canary right now and post perf deltas
  2) kevin: implement probe upsample rule for kv_warm<0.4
  3) chen: add `triton_route_switch_count` and `triton_p99_tail` metrics + tiny alert
chen: SGTM. I'll create the metric + alert: trigger if triton_p99_tail > 150ms for 5m.
aj: Starting canary now :rocket:
runtime-bot: deploy started for router-policy at 1779992505
marta: Thanks — I'll watch the token-level dashboard (per-route latency + kv_warm) and post updates. If we see sustained tail, we'll roll back the probe bias change.
kevin: One more note: collect raw kernel durations (histogram buckets) from the tracer for the canary window so we can attribute tail sources (queue vs kernel vs preempt).
marta: noted. I'll also log a short postmortem template if this recurs. Will follow up with PRs for the metric additions and probe rule changes.
